material_scars.finding: The first source strategy globally rejected U+200B/U+2060/U+FEFF because they are invisible.
material_scars.repair: Primary Unicode evidence showed these characters have legitimate line-breaking/BOM semantics. The strategy was replaced, not cosmetically retried: source is preserved and an explicit evidence projection reveals invisible semantics without making acceptance decisions.

material_scars.finding: The first reveal projection used human-readable inline markers without reserving a marker namespace, so literal source marker text could alias an actual invisible code point in the diagnostic display.
material_scars.repair: Backslash is now the marker introducer and literal source backslashes are doubled. Actual U+200B and literal source spelling \u{200B ZWSP} now produce distinct projections.

primary_unicode_review: Unicode Standard 17.0 Chapter 23 documents U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE as a word/line-break opportunity including use in languages without visible word spacing.
Unicode Standard Annex #14 documents U+2060 WORD JOINER as the preferred invisible character for preventing a line break and records FEFF/ZWNBSP behavior.
Existing heartbeat policy already preserves ZWJ; this slice also protects ZWNJ language shaping from blanket-format rejection.
